items.bodyExcerpt:
### What does this PR do?

Depends on:
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51368
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52552
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52626
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53361
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56327
- https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/pull/6044
- https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7054
- https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7521
- https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7522
- https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7523

Adds DeepSeek V4 (DSV4) LoRA support to verl's vLLM weight-sync path. Previously a merge=False LoRA base sync orphaned the `.base_layer.` suffix on wrapped modules and mishandled the mxfp4 quant path, so DSV4 LoRA diverged from the actor.

This reworks weight-name reconciliation to be runtime-probed (strict vs flat loader) instead of model-type-based, unwraps the LoRA-installed mxfp4 quant-method wrapper, and threads `peft_config` through the FP8/mxfp4 load path so the same reconciliation applies there.

Tested with Megatron backend, GPU E2E (DSV4 merge=F GRPO, 2-node): step1/step2 pearson 0.9970/0.9950, aligned to run15 merge=T 0.9952/0.9944.

items.title: Port PR #55738 (GLM-5.3-Flash NoPE MLA prefill) to older vLLM trees + SM120 note
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Context

vLLM PR #55738 (merged 2026-09-14) adds GLM-5.3-Flash's NoPE MLA layout
(`qk_nope_head_dim=256, qk_rope_head_dim=0, v_head_dim=256`) to the
FlashAttention MLA prefill allow-list and the masked-MHA availability check,
plus a short-circuit for the no-op `k_pe` concat.

We applied the equivalent changes to an **older vLLM tree**
(`glm53-sm120nope` image, vLLM `0.1.dev20051+g487ecf187`, built 2026-08-27)
running GLM-5.3-Flash on 8x RTX PRO 6000 (SM120). This document is the exact
patch content we applied, as a portable reference for others on older trees.
It also documents an important caveat we measured: **if your deployment still
shows `No MLA prefill backend supports this model`, you are leaving large
prefill throughput on the table — this patch is the fix.**

## Files touched (3)

### 1. `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py`

In `_concat_k_nope_k_pe`, right after the docstring:

```python
        if k_pe.shape[-1] == 0:
            # NoPE MLA: nothing to append, so no copy either.
            return k_nope
```

Rationale: GLM-5.3-Flash has `qk_rope_head_dim=0`, so `k_pe` is
zero-width; the concat allocates a full tensor and copies for nothing
on every layer, every step.

### 2. `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/sparse_mla_attention.py`

`_is_masked_mha_available` — allow the GLM NoPE dims through the
availability gate. On the older tree the check is an inequality chain
(upstream #55738 refactored it into a tuple set); the equivalent
rewrite is:

```python

            and qk_nope_head_dim == 256 and qk_rope_head_dim == 0 and v_head_dim == 256)
    )
    if not valid:
        return False
```

items.title: [Bug] GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 + MTP: draft layer is BF16 in the checkpoint but vLLM builds its experts NVFP4-packed (128 vs 256 weight-load crash)
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

`nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` (the NVIDIA modelopt NVFP4 package) fails at startup when speculative decoding is enabled, in the MTP draft layer's expert weight loading. Present on `0.30.1rc1.dev511` and latest nightly `dev619+g5f30fc703`.

```
File "vllm/models/glm5next/common/mtp.py", line 386, in load_weights
  success = weight_loader(...)
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/routed_experts.py", in _load_w2
  expert_data.copy_(loaded_weight)
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (128) must match the size of tensor b (256) at non-singleton dimension 1
```

## Root cause (verified against the checkpoint bytes)

The package quantizes only the main-model layers; the **nextn/MTP draft layer (`model.language_model.layers.45.*`, num_hidden_layers=44) stays BF16**:

- main experts (e.g. layers.3): modelopt NVFP4 triple — `down_proj.weight` U8 `[4096, 1024]` packed + `F8_E4M3 [4096, 128]` scales + F32 global scale → per-TP8-rank slice `[4096, 128]`, matching the packed expert buffer
- draft experts (layers.45): plain `BF16 [4096, 2048]`, **no scale tensors** → per-rank slice `[4096, 256]` vs the NVFP4-packed buffer `[4096, 128]` → the 128 vs 256 crash

`Glm5NextMTP` builds the draft's MoE from the **global** `quant_config`, so the draft expert buffers are NVFP4-packed even though the checkpoint's draft layer is excluded from quantization (modelopt `exclude_modules`, 132 entries). Without `--speculative-config` the model loads and serves correctly (FLASHINFER_CUTLASS NvFp4 MoE, correct output), so the bug is specifically the draft layer's quant-awareness.

## Reproduction

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 8   --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'   --max-model-len 32768   # crash at weight load on every TP rank
```

## Suggested fix direction

When constructing the draft layer's MoE, honor the checkpoint's per-layer quantization: if the modelopt config's `exclude_modules` covers the nextn layer (

items.title: fix: convert LogprobsLists to lists for cross node Ray transport (#38602)
items.bodyExcerpt:
Closes #38602.

## What's broken

Production deployment of GLM 5.1 FP8 on TP=8 + PP=2 across two nodes hangs deterministically the moment any request includes `logprobs:true`. The same prompt without logprobs returns in seconds. GPUs sit at 0% for the entire duration of the hang. No traceback is ever logged, no NCCL warning, no kernel event. After roughly 900 seconds the engine finally crashes with `ray.exceptions.RayChannelTimeoutError` on the cross node compiled DAG return channel and the deployment goes unhealthy.

This reproduces with `distributed_executor_backend=ray` and the V1 engine on any two node Ray cluster where the model has TP > 1 and PP > 1. Any client that sets logprobs (LangChain probability aware chains, eval harnesses, RAG re rankers, agentic frameworks doing token level confidence scoring) silently bricks the deployment.

## Where the hang is

I traced this with line level instrumentation along the logprobs path:

```
WORKER NODE (8 RayWorkerWrappers, last PP stage):
  M1..M5  sampler.forward fires through gather_logprobs        x 8
  M5a..e  bookkeeping, tolists() returned                      x 8
  M5f..g  _get_prompt_logprobs_dict ok                         x 8
  M5h..k  eplb_step, ModelRunnerOutput constructed, returned   x 8

DRIVER (head, EngineCore):
  M13     FutureWrapper.result: ray.get starting               x 1
  M14     FutureWrapper.result: ray.get returned               x 0   <-- HANG
```

The worker fully constructs and returns `ModelRunnerOutput`. The driver's `ray.get` on the compiled DAG return ref never resolves.

To prove the hang is in transport, not compute, I set `model_runner_output.logprobs = None` after the worker computed it. Result: HTTP 200 in 1.8 seconds, M14 fires. That isolates the wedge to transmission of `LogprobsLists` (a `NamedTuple` containing three numpy ndarrays) across the cross node Ray channel.

Full bisect trace and the nullification experiment are in the issue thread.

Two changes, 2 files,

## Summary

Adds reasoning + tool parsers for the **`naver-hyperclovax/HyperCLOVAX-SEED-Think-32B`** model, targeting the model's actual published chat template (`</think>` boundary + XML `<tool_call>` format).

Two new parser modules, each registered via the existing lazy-loading tables
(`_REASONING_PARSERS_TO_REGISTER` / `_TOOL_PARSERS_TO_REGISTER`).

## Files

- `vllm/reasoning/hyperclovax_seed_think_reasoning_parser.py` (new, ~180 lines)
- `vllm/tool_parsers/hyperclovax_seed_think_tool_parser.py` (new, ~410 lines)
- `vllm/reasoning/__init__.py` (+4 lines, lazy table entry)
- `vllm/tool_parsers/__init__.py` (+4 lines, lazy table entry)
- `tests/reasoning/test_hyperclovax_seed_think_reasoning_parser.py` (new, 26 unit tests)
- `tests/tool_parsers/test_hyperclovax_seed_think_tool_parser.py` (new, 23 unit tests)

## Model output formats

### Reasoning (chat_template controlled by `chat_template_kwargs.thinking`)
- `thinking=true` → generation prompt ends with `<think>\n`; model emits
  `[reasoning]</think>\n\n[content]`.
- `thinking=false` → prompt already contains `<think>\n\n</think>\n\n`;
  model emits `[content]` directly.

### Tool calls (per chat_template's system prompt)
```
<tool_call>{function-name}
<arg_key>{k1}</arg_key>
<arg_value>{v1}</arg_value>
...
</tool_call>
```

For `tool_choice="required"` / named tool_choice, vLLM's default
`adjust_request` injects a JSON list schema. With `thinking=true` the
schema engages after `</think>` and the model outputs
`[{"name": ..., "parameters": {...}}]` instead of the XML form. The tool
parser accepts both formats; non-streaming via `extract_tool_calls`,
streaming via `_emit_json_tool_calls`.

Mirrors the GLM / Qwen3Coder pattern for XML-emitting tool models:

items.title: [CI][Docs] Fix decode/prefill consistency test prefix construction; add GLM-4-9B and Phi-4 to batch-invariant tested models
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Two related changes, both following the review on this PR:

1. **Fix a soundness bug in `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_decode_logprobs_match_prefill_logprobs`.** The test rebuilt each prefill prefix from *text* and re-encoded it; `encode(decode(ids))` is not lossless for BPE tokenizers, so the "prefill" could evaluate a different token sequence than decode did and report false mismatches. The prefix is now built directly from token ids (`prompt_token_ids + decode_token_ids[:i]`), which also removes an O(N²) extra `llm.generate` per decoded token. This is the fix from #43317 (@Evangade), carried here at the maintainer's request after that PR went stale; the standalone tokenizer regression test from #43317 is dropped per the review there. Original report by @xRay2016 in #27433.
2. **Add `zai-org/glm-4-9b-chat` and `microsoft/phi-4` to the tested-model list**, following the [invitation to submit model validations without a separate issue](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53247#issuecomment-5374419058).

Why the fix matters here: GLM was originally removed from this PR because the official suite reported a decode/prefill mismatch. Root cause (see the comments below): the model emits `'.'` + `'Here'` as `[13, 8419]`, which re-encodes to the single token `89329` (`'.Here'`), so the text-based prefix diverged from position 11 onward. With token-id prefixes GLM is fully green. Any model whose greedy output hits a BPE merge point can false-fail the unfixed test the same way.

Not a duplicate: #43317 proposes the same test fix but has had no author activity since the May review and is marked stale; this PR carries that commit with its original authorship and sign-off instead of opening another PR.

## Test Plan

Official suite, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, vLLM 0.28.0 (cu129 wheel), torch 2.13.0, Triton 3.7.1, RTX 4090 D (sm89) and H20 (sm90):

items.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Honor modality-scoped mm_processor_kwargs in every model that reads them
items.bodyExcerpt:
> **Update 2026-10-03:** `get_image_size_with_most_features` is now sized per modality (image by default, video for video tokens). See "The size bound follows the modality being sized" below.

> **Update 2026-09-30:** #56372 removed `get_merged_mm_kwargs(..., modality=)`, which the text below describes. The reads now go through `InputProcessingContext.get_modality_mm_kwargs(kwargs, modality)`: the resolved kwargs, with that modality's scope overlaid for vLLM-side reads. Each call site's change is otherwise unchanged. `mistral3` and `qwen2_5_omni_thinker` now match `main` (#56372 fixed mistral3 itself). Details and a fresh test run: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54527#issuecomment-5905006141

Follow-up to #53808.

## Background

#53808 taught `get_merged_mm_kwargs` to overlay HF-style nested
`images_kwargs` / `videos_kwargs` / `audio_kwargs` onto the flat namespace, and
threaded a `modality` argument through Qwen2-VL and Qwen3-VL. Its docstring
states the rule:

> When `modality` is set, HF-style nested `images_kwargs` / `videos_kwargs` /
> `audio_kwargs` are overlaid onto the flat namespace for vLLM-side reads
> (token budgets, dummy inputs). Processor construction and HF `__call__`
> should omit `modality` so the nested dicts still reach the HF processor.

Every model outside the Qwen family that predicts sizes or token counts from
those kwargs was left reading the flat namespace only. The HF processor honors
the nested dict in its `__call__`, so vLLM and the processor disagree about how
many tokens an item expands to.

## Scope: every call site audited

Per review this now covers every multi-modal model, not just the VL three.
I enumerated every `get_merged_mm_kwargs` call site and classified each (40 when
this PR was opened, 44 on current `main`).

| model | site | modality |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `glm4_1v` | `_get_image_max_pixels`, `_get_video_max_pixels` | static |

## Purpose

Addresses the identity-entry resolution reported in #54641 by @stefanskiasan. (The
`amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` checkpoint that surfaced it needs #56176 instead — see *Scope*.)

An identity entry in `packed_modules_mapping` (a module mapped to itself, e.g.
`"gate_up_proj": ["gate_up_proj"]`) silently disables `layer_quant_config` for that module. The
layer falls back to `global_quant_config`, so a mixed-precision Quark checkpoint that names the
module is built with the wrong scheme and only fails later, at weight load, with a shape mismatch.

Identity entries exist because the checkpoint really stores the fused tensor: GLM-4.1V ships a
pre-fused `gate_up_proj`, which is why `Glm4vForConditionalGeneration` maps it to itself. A Quark
checkpoint of such a model keys `layer_quant_config` by that fused name, and today that entry is
ignored.

**Scope.** This does *not* fix `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4`: that config keys the split
`gate_proj` / `up_proj` names (none `gate_up_proj`), and the actual bug there is the identity
mapping `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` inherits from GLM-4.1V although GLM-5.3-Flash stores
gate/up separately — fixed by the mapping override in #56176. Once the mapping expands to real
shards, the branch this PR changes is not reached; the two are complementary. The reporter's
locally produced config named the fused module (the trace in #54641 shows the key present but
`hit=False`), which is exactly the path fixed here.

Both lookup paths in `QuarkConfig` treat `shard_name == layer_name` as "no shard information":

```python
# get_layer_quant_config_from_name
if shard_name != layer_name:
    config = self.get_layer_quant_config_from_name(shard_name)
else:
    config = None              # identity entry -> no config

# _find_matched_config
if shard_name == layer_name:
    config = fallback_config   # identity entry -> global scheme
```

That guard is only there to stop the recursion, since substituting an identity entry is a no-op.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Follow-up to merged #55277: use compact 528-byte `fp8_ds_mla` rows for native NoPE on the FlashInfer SM120 backend. Rebased onto upstream main `e6674262f1`. Only tests conflicted: #55528 made the MLA KV-spec test's fake layer carry `attn_backend`, and the HiSparse test helper gained `max_union_rows`; both were resolved by keeping both sides. The two commits are now `aab1e922fa` and `e879b2ef44` (head), and the branch merges cleanly into current main.

The row contains 512 FP8 latent bytes and four FP32 group scales. There is no RoPE payload. A single backend-owned row-size method supplies both the KV spec and early HiSparse registration. On SM120, compact selection depends solely on `kv_lora_rank=512` and `qk_rope_head_dim=0`, independent of model name, connector, or offloading configuration. Other backend layouts are unchanged; real RoPE64 `fp8_ds_mla` retains 656-byte rows. No new dtype or CLI option is added.

The writer accepts NoPE 528/656, preserves legacy zero-tail behavior for 656, and rejects RoPE64 with 528. It distinguishes logical row width from physical stride. The fixed 576-dimensional gather rejects compact input. HiSparse uses actual row widths for byte movement and rejects incompatible shared-staging layouts.

No connector changes, layout negotiation, or old-cache migration are added. Local prefix caching remains supported. External connectors were not tested end to end.

Duplicate-work check: #53969/#55778/#55543 use padded compatibility layouts; #55219/#57169 address broader paging/stride plumbing, not this compact writer/spec change. items.title: [Core] Add --release-weight-page-cache to drop checkpoint pages after load
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Problem

A DEP32 GLM-5.3 prefill group (4 pods x 8 DP ranks, DeepEP) dies as a unit: one rank stops between steps, the other 31 wait for it in `internode_dispatch`, hit the 100 s DeepEP timeout and trap (Xid 43); the stalled rank never traps. Captured on a production group right after its first real requests:

- The stalled worker's main thread was in kernel state `D` inside `__vm_munmap` for 73 s, ran for 1 s, then in a 16 KiB anonymous `mmap` (`vm_mmap_pgoff`) for 88 s. `py-spy` could not attach for exactly that window, since it needs `mmap_lock` as well.
- `perf` on the same workers under load: 1,000-3,400 `mmap` + `munmap` calls per second per worker, all 16 KiB. CPython 3.12 allocates a new frame data-stack chunk with `mmap` when a call crosses the end of the current chunk and frees it on return (python/cpython#142183, fixed in 3.13.13); the MoE forward crosses that boundary in every layer.
- The node sat at its free-memory floor for the whole stall: MemFree 16 GiB against MemAvailable 896 GiB (about 700 GiB of clean checkpoint pages plus a 761 GiB CPU KV tier in shm), with direct-reclaim bursts (`pgscan_direct` 7k-20k per 5 s), `compact_stall` 23-56 per 5 s and hundreds of `thp_fault_fallback`. MemFree jumped from 17 to 344 GiB the moment the group died.

`mmap` and `munmap` take the process `mmap_lock` for write; a page fault takes it for read and, with no free pages, holds it through direct reclaim and compaction. One faulting thread in reclaim blocks the main thread's chunk `munmap`, and the queued writer then blocks every later fault in the process, so the whole worker stops. The condition exists whenever a pod starts on a node whose previous pod left the checkpoint in the page cache (any in-place restart or rollout) and is worst on a rank's first real requests, when the KV tier faults in new pages at scale.

items.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Fix GLM-5.3-Flash vision tower crashes on image input
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix two independent ways an image request takes down the engine in the GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`) vision tower.

**1. Every image trips the GPU sync check.** `rot_pos_emb` builds `pos_ids` on the host and copied it with `.to(device, non_blocking=True)` from pageable memory, and the eager `forward` did the same with `cu_seqlens`. A non-blocking copy from pageable memory can block the host, so with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` the first image raises `Implicit GPU<->CPU sync detected - use a pinned, densely laid out CPU tensor, or wrap with gpu_sync_allowed()` and the engine dies.

Fix: stage both copies through pinned memory with `async_tensor_h2d`, as `Glm4vVisionTransformer` does for its position tables. The eager and CUDA-graph forward paths are otherwise unchanged. The `max_seqlen` read-back in the ViT attention wrappers already runs under `gpu_sync_allowed()`, so nothing else in the eager path trips the check.

**2. Slim images overflow the vision rope table.** Since vllm-project/vllm#57387, images go through the transformers `Glm5NextImageProcessor`, whose `smart_resize` bounds them by token budget only, with no aspect-ratio cap. A slim image therefore gets a grid side beyond the hardcoded `max_position=8192`. For example, with the checkpoint's `processor_config.json`, a 200000×20 px image is accepted at 7143 tokens with `image_grid_thw = [1, 2, 14286]`, and `cos[pos_ids]` reads past the table: an `IndexError` on CPU, a device-side assert on GPU.

Fix (suggested in review): size the table from `text_config.max_position_embeddings`. For GLM-5.3-Flash that is 1,048,576 rows, about 64 MiB in bf16 per GPU.

For every grid that fit the old table, the vision tower's output is bit-identical to before.

Neither bug depends on quantization or KV-cache dtype: the tower is built with `quant_config=None` and uses no KV cache, and the `RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` vision weights are BF16, as in `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`.

items.title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Measure the CUDA graph pool for the memory estimate, not the capture's free-memory delta
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #59318.

`profile_cudagraph_memory()` (model runner V2, #53306) sizes the KV cache budget with two numbers that are not graph memory:

1. `measured` is the free-memory delta of `capture_model(profile_only=True)`. It also counts the first-use allocations the pass makes outside the graph pool (on GLM-5.3 TP4/DCP4 about 1.0 GiB of non-torch memory per rank: NCCL, JIT modules) and the transients the caching allocator keeps. The real capture later pays neither, because the profiling pass already made them.
2. The FULL extrapolation `first + (N - 1) * mem_samples[1]` samples per-graph free-memory deltas, and those deltas are negative: `torch.cuda.graph.__enter__` calls `empty_cache()` before every capture, so each sample is "pool growth minus the cache released from the previous warmup". `per_graph` is then floored to 1 MiB, and `measured - sum(mem_samples)` adds back the absolute value of the second sample (0.37 GiB here). The 0.40 GiB gap in the issue is that sign artifact, not a slope problem; the instrumented run below shows the 16 smaller FULL graphs add 0 bytes to the pool after the first one.

The issue's decomposition of the 0.97 GiB was right on part 1 and wrong on the mechanism of part 2; the numbers are in the test results.

This PR:

- captures every descriptor in the profiling pass (FULL graphs are cheap: 4 s for 17 here) and drops the sampling and extrapolation;
- measures the throwaway pool through the allocator snapshot (`segment_pool_id`) instead of the free-memory delta, with the delta kept as a fallback where there is no snapshot;
- reserves, on top of the pool, what the pass still holds after teardown (`free before - free after teardown`), and stores it as `runner.cudagraph_profiling_retained_bytes`. That memory is real process footprint the profile run never saw; before this PR it was charged by accident as part of the delta. It is logged as its own line item so it can be argued about separately;

items.title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Pass per-sequence context lengths to the AITER paged MQA-logits kernels
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Error

MTP with native DSA-indexer decode above `next_n=2` crashes during warm-up on MI355X (seen at `next_n=3` and `next_n=6`). GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP4, `num_speculative_tokens=5` (`next_n=6`), Gluon paged MQA logits:

```
Memory access fault by GPU node-4 (Agent handle: 0x20465ea0) on address 0x792dc0bf1000. Reason: Unknown.
```

Where it does not crash, the indexer silently uses wrong causal bounds: in a direct call at `next_n=3`, the 8192-token sequence loses its last 2 valid positions in every row (9/12 rows correct).

## Cause

With native decode (`next_n > 1`), `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` receives a `(B, next_n)` table of per-row context lengths, `[b, j] = L_b - next_n + j + 1`, built in [`indexer.py#L1136-L1152`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2df122e65e87dc12870ce5f0180b49f012e7a53b/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py#L1136-L1152). The AITER Gluon `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` and `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1` kernels read the table as a flat `[B]` array and some sequences get another row's length.

Example: 4 requests, `next_n=3`, context lengths 8192 / 1500 / 3000 / 700:

| `b` | `j=0` | `j=1` | `j=2` | `L_b` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 8190 | 8191 | **8192** | 8192 |
| 1 | 1498 | 1499 | **1500** | 1500 |
| 2 | 2998 | 2999 | **3000** | 3000 |
| 3 | 698 | 699 | **700** | 700 |

The kernel expects `[8192, 1500, 3000, 700]` and computes each row's bound itself. Reading the `(4, 3)` table as `[4]`, it gets the first four values in memory, `[8190, 8191, 8192, 1498]`: request 0 loses its last 2 positions in every row, and requests 1 to 3 get lengths past their own KV pages, the likely source of the fault. Column `j = next_n - 1` equals `L_b`, which is what the kernel needs.

## Fix

Pass the kernels the last column, which is the per-sequence length. `[B]` and `(B, 1)` inputs, the C4A Triton path and the torch fallback are unchanged.

## Purpose

Uses the AITER FlyDSL paged (decode) MQA-logits kernel for the sparse indexer on gfx950 when AITER provides it, instead of the Gluon kernel. No new env var, same as #59280 for prefill and #49544 for gfx942.

items.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Fall back to free text in the GLM-4.7 structural tag without function tools
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Since #56403, every GLM-4.7 request with tools gets the shallow structural tag by default. A Responses request whose tools are all builtin (`mcp`, `web_search`, ...) has no function tool to build a tag for, so the builder emits `TriggeredTagsFormat(tags=[])`, which xgrammar rejects. Such requests now fail with `400 Invalid structural tag specification` instead of generating text as they did before #56403.

## Claims

- GLM-4.7 (`glm_4_7` structural tag model, also used by `ling3`) with `tool_choice="auto"` and no function tools falls back to free text, as the xgrammar builtin and the `hermes` tag already do.
- No change for requests with at least one function tool, or for `required` / named tool choice.

## Validation

Repro on `main` (CPU only):

## Validation

GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4, TP4 prefill -> TP4 decode on one host (4+4 RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, two NUMA halves), Mooncake over RDMA, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 65536 --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192`, one run each:

items.title: [Feature][DCP] Gather-based DCP for MLA attention without native DCP (+ DSv4)
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Draft: a backend-agnostic, gather-based DCP for MLA models that can't run DCP natively. It is an alternative to layer-sharded KV (KVPP, #59059). It also includes two bug fixes found while validating it: DCP group rank order under PCP, and the DSv3.2/GLM top-k across PP stages.

## Claims

- **Gather DCP.** With `-dcp N`, MLA models whose attention backend can't run the configured DCP now gather the block-sharded KV per layer instead of failing. Examples: GLM-5.3 at TP2/TP4 with FlashMLA sparse (≥32 local heads or a2a), dense MLA under PCP, DeepSeek-V4. Attention backends are unmodified. `--force-dcp-gather` opts in where native DCP works.
- **Performance.** On GLM-5.3-NVFP4 prefill it matches KVPP throughput with more KV capacity. At TP4 it is 1.55x native TP4×DCP4.
- **DeepSeek-V4-Flash** gets DCP (TP2/TP4) at baseline accuracy.
- **Fix: DCP group rank order.** TP2×PCP2×DCP4 (DCP spanning TP×PCP) served garbage on main (GSM8K 0.000 → 0.905).
- **Fix: top-k across PP stages.** PP2 on GLM-5.3 split a top-k-sharing layer group across stages, so stage 1 read a stale top-k (gather PP2×TP2 0.820 → 0.908).
